notes:
Summary: Orchid Reserve Systems (FinServ analytics) evaluating Redwood Dedicated for customer-facing personalization & support-chat. Primary ask: reserved GPU pool across multi-region with clear failover headroom and contractual throughput/latency SLOs.

Sales notes / call snippets:
- C-level: 'We cannot tolerate >200ms p95 on search/retrieval in prime markets' — latency is a legal/UX requirement for their trading desk portal.
- Engineering: pref to keep KV cache warm across AZs, want prefix caching + cross-region replication plan.
- Security: must support SSO/SAML, KMS key ownership, and audit logs shipped to their SIEM.
- Procurement: wants example commitment schedules and a clear credit model for downtime > SLA.

Sizing ask (customer-provided):
- Baseline production: 16k concurrent sessions (avg 1.8k tokens/sec per session spike pattern) — peak QPS pattern concentrated in NA and EU.
- Requested reserved pool: plan for 48 A100-class equivalents split across 3 regions (US-EAST, US-WEST, EU-WEST) with an additional 20% failover headroom (effective reserve ~58 GPUs) for AZ-level and region-level outages.
- Target throughput guarantee: sustained 120k tokens/sec across the pooled capacity, burst to 250k tokens/sec for short spikes (up to 60s) with autoscaling/Burst credits.
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 160ms for 2048 tokens context on chat endpoint; p95 < 120ms for reranking endpoints.
- Preferred models: open Llama-family variants for embeddings/rerank; allow quantized 4-bit options if accuracy delta < 1.5% on evals.

Operational constraints:
- Data residency: EU customer data must remain in EU region for EU users; routing policy required.
- Wants deterministic rollout windows and canary traffic split for model upgrades.
- Recovery objective: regional failover target < 180s to full degraded capacity, with automatic routing to secondary region; customer wants runbook for manual failover too.

Recent engagement summary: Diego presented dedicated cost model and failover architecture on 2026-02-18. Security SOW draft shared 2026-03-02. Legal asked for SLA credit examples 2026-03-05.

Quotes & red flags: 'We'll accept some quantization but need eval against our fairness/regulatory test suite' — SE note.

CRM shorthand: heavy procurement, exec sponsor = CTO (R. Patel), need legal + infra buy-in.

sizing_requirements: Customer prefers an explicit reserved pool plan: allocate GPUs across 3 regions with per-region minimums (US-EAST 22, EU-WEST 16, US-WEST 10) and a 20% cross-region failover buffer. Wants explicit AZ diversity (no single-AZ > 40% of region capacity). Require ability to schedule planned maintenance with 14-day notice and transparent expected throughput impact.
throughput_latency_targets: Sustained throughput guarantee: 120k tokens/sec pooled. Burst to 250k tokens/sec for up to 60s. Latency SLOs: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 160ms for chat (2048 ctx). Reranking p95 < 120ms. Must include stated measurement method (end-to-end including network + queuing).
failover_headroom_policy: Customer expects minimum 20% reserved headroom to cover region outage; require automatic re-routing with capacity throttles and explicit fallbacks to quantized model variants when capacity constrained. Wants documented warm-cache replication approach and estimated cold-start window per AZ.
sla_negotiation_notes: Key asks: uptime SLA >= 99.9% per region for dedicated pool; credits scalable with duration/impact tiers. Orchid legal pushing for MTTR <= 30 minutes for critical endpoints; Redwood team suggests 1 hour with automated fallback guarantees. Customer requests trial month with documented SLA credits and a run-rate commitment option. Need to draft amendment with explicit throughput guarantees and credit table.
po_checklist: Needed: finalized reserve sizing worksheet, legal SLA addendum, KMS integration plan, SOC2 scope confirmation, billing cadence. Procurement needs a sample SOW with ramp schedule and termination clauses tied to committed GPUs.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: under-provisioned reserve causing repeated fallbacks -> Mitigation: add 20% buffer + automatic tiered fallback and telemetry alerts. Risk: SLA language too broad on credits -> Mitigation: propose tiered credit matrix and a 30-day proof-of-capacity pilot. Risk: data residency gaps -> Mitigation: per-route routing policy and VPC peering with regional enforcement.
